subtopic: Learning to code from the internet
subtype: Approach: joining a study group for accountability [Action]
passage: Coding club teacher's note, Friday. Samir has been meeting two classmates in the library every Friday at 4:15. The rule: each person solves one problem during the week and presents the solution to the other two. Week three was a dull one, with exams and heat, and I saw Samir skip. The others didn't scold. One sent a message: “We start at 4:15, need your loop.” Samir turned up with half a solution, and the three finished it together. Nobody has missed since. All I did was give them a corner and a whiteboard. Samir told me, “If it were only me, I'd have quit in week three.” — Zainab

qa.q: When does the study group meet?
What might Samir be feeling when admitting to quitting in week three without the group?
qa.a: Grateful and a bit relieved: the group's nudge kept Samir going through a dull week.

qa.q: What else could the group do to keep going, and why?
qa.a: Take turns choosing the weekly problem, since shared ownership keeps everyone invested.

qa.q: How does the group look to the classmate who sent the message?
qa.a: That classmate probably feels responsible for the group and glad Samir came, and the kind nudge kept it friendly instead of scolding.

grounding: A student teams with two classmates to solve and present one problem a week and nudge whoever skips.
